Article Title: Harshit Rana ruled out as Yash Thakur named replacement for Afghanistan T20Is, Asian Games
Article Text:
Harshit Rana and Yash Thakur (Agency Image)

India squad for the 2026 Asian Games: S

NEW DELHI: India fast bowler Harshit Rana has been ruled out of the upcoming T20I series against Afghanistan and the 2026 Asian Games after suffering another injury setback, with Vidarbha pacer Yash Thakur named as his replacement in both squads.As TimesofIndia.com had earlier reported, Rana had been progressing well with his rehabilitation at the BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE), but suffered a rectus femoris strain while bowling during a match simulation on September 7. Following the setback, the Men's Selection Committee ruled him out of the upcoming assignments.The development comes after a prolonged injury layoff for Rana. The fast bowler sustained a hamstring injury during the third T20I against England at Trent Bridge earlier this year.He also injured his knee during India's warm-up match against South Africa ahead of the 2026 Men's T20 World Cup and was ruled out of the tournament. Rana then underwent surgery and missed the 2026 Indian Premier League, where he was part of the Kolkata Knight Riders squad.After completing his rehabilitation, Rana was brought back into India's plans and was added to the squad for the third ODI against Afghanistan in Chennai on June 20.The latest injury, however, has forced him out of India's next two assignments.Rana's absence will be a blow to a pace attack that already includes Jasprit Bumrah and Arshdeep Singh. The selectors have opted for Yash Thakur as his replacement, handing the Vidarbha pacer another opportunity at international level.Yash Thakur gets another India call-upThe 27-year-old Thakur recently made his T20I debut during India's tour of Zimbabwe in July. He featured in two matches and picked up four wickets.His domestic record has also made him a regular name in India's limited-overs plans. Thakur has played 50 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy matches and has taken 81 wickets at an economy rate of 7.04.He will now be part of India's squads for both the Afghanistan T20I series and the Asian Games.India will face Afghanistan in a three-match T20I series on September 13, 15 and 17. Although all three matches will be played in Delhi, Afghanistan are the official hosts of the bilateral series.India will then turn their attention to the 2026 Asian Games. The team is scheduled to depart from Delhi on September 18, with Iyer continuing as captain and Tilak as vice-captain.Shreyas Iyer [C], Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Sanju Samson [WK], Ishan Kishan [WK], Tilak Varma [VC], Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Varun Chakaravarthy, Ravi Bishnoi, Jasprit Bumrah, Arshdeep Singh, Yash Thakurhreyas Iyer (C), Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson (WK), Ishan Kishan (WK), Shivam Dube, Tilak Varma (VC), Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Varun Chakaravarthy, Ravi Bishnoi, Jasprit Bumrah, Arshdeep Singh, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Yash Thakur
Article Summary: Harshit Rana ruled out of T20I series against Afghanistan and 2026 Asian Games. Vidarbha pacer Yash Thakur named as his replacement in both squads. Rana suffered a rectus femoris strain while bowling during a match simulation.

Article Title: Chess by day, Salem by night: Board games, tennis and Nihal Sarin's 7 am GCL night
Article Text:
Nihal Sarin in GCL (Photo by GCL)

Chess Olympiad in focus

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Vidit Gujrathi (FIDE Photo)

BENGALURU: The ITC Windsor hotel, home to the six teams competing in the 2026 Global Chess League (GCL), sits at the heart of the city. Walk in after the security check at the gate, past doormen greeting you with folded hands, and a left turn down the hallway from reception leads to the dining area, where Dutch No. 1 Anish Giri can be found sipping a hot chocolate latte beside his Alpine Pipers teammate and close friend Vidit Gujrathi. Look towards the other corner and Levon Aronian and Maxime Vachier-Lagrave are reading the morning newspaper.For Nihal Sarin, the most effective player for the American Gambits so far this season, the time on the clock matters little here. For him, it is still midnight. And why wouldn't it be? "We stayed up till around 7 am," Nihal told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive interaction on Wednesday. "We were playing a board game called Salem. It's a social deduction game."Among those who stayed up late with him was his American Gambits teammate and World Championship challenger Javokhir Sindarov, an avowed video game enthusiast who, by his own admission, played Counter-Strike between rounds during his Candidates win in Cyprus earlier this year. "Sindarov is a good friend of mine, very humble, and down to earth.He is very chill and always smiling," the 22-year-old added.Video games, however, have never held the same pull for Nihal. Suggest a game of padel or a board game instead, and he'll be the first to put his hand up.Tuesday's late night, though, wasn't about squeezing in one more round of board games. It was about waiting up for the US Open men's quarterfinal between Ben Shelton and Carlos Alcaraz.But even staying awake till 7 am wasn't quite enough; the match was delayed after the preceding women's quarterfinal between Jessica Pegula and Emma Navarro ran long, and Nihal, a long-time tennis fan, eventually lost his battle with sleep.Amid a schedule that has him playing almost two games of intense rapid chess almost every day, Nihal hasn't lost track of the sport he has followed for years. And what about the Williams sisters' return to professional tennis? "I didn't expect that at all," he said while raising both his eyebrows. "The tendency to even compete at that level at that age is truly extraordinary."For Nihal, anyone who has been at the top of their game and is still putting in the work to prove it deserves to be called an "absolute legend."In the context of the GCL, that applies just as much to five-time World Champion Viswanathan Anand , who has had a quiet season for his new team, Alaskan Knights. The 56-year-old has been winless in six games, with only two draws. But the poor form hasn't dented his legacy as a chess icon even a bit in Nihal's eyes."People are there to take shots at him, but Vishy doesn't give a crap about their opinion. And that is why he is a legend," Nihal said. "The FIDE role and everything don't matter much here, but the way he has performed in some of these games here is simply outstanding at this age."Nihal is part of the Indian team preparing to defend its Open title at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, later this month, which will also be his first appearance in India's main Olympiad squad.He is, by his own description, excited and thrilled about it."I am very happy because we are all friends and have been together from the start, except for Vidit," he quipped. "He is the old one, not from our generation. But jokes aside, Vidit is a top player who has already won gold for India at that level (Olympiad)."Grandmaster and coach Srinath Narayanan led an intense pre-Olympiad training camp for the Indian team in late August to prepare for Samarkand. Nihal was a part of it.While the Kerala-born Grandmaster did not reveal many details about the camp, he acknowledged, “Virtual camps are not as helpful as in-person ones. But I am very much excited for the Olympiad,” before signing off casually, “I will go and take a nap after my breakfast.” It was already 2:30 pm on the clock.
Article Summary: Nihal Sarin is part of the Indian team preparing to defend its Open title at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, later this month. The 22-year-old has been playing almost two games of intense rapid chess almost every day. Nihal was a part of India's pre-Olympiad training camp in Kerala.

Article Title: Masked protesters mistake Pakistan U-19 cricket team for asylum seekers in Portsmouth
Article Text:
Pakistan U-19 cricket team

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A group of masked protesters gathered outside a four-star hotel in Portsmouth after wrongly believing that a group of asylum seekers had been taken there. They later discovered that the people staying at the hotel were members of Pakistan's Under-19 cricket team.Around 40 people gathered outside the Marriott hotel on Tuesday evening, with many wearing balaclavas or other face coverings. The protesters had reportedly seen a group of men they believed were asylum seekers arriving at the hotel.George Madgwick, a Reform councillor whose ward includes the hotel, was called to the scene to help resolve the situation. He spoke to the hotel manager, who explained that the men were Pakistan's Under-19 cricketers, who are in England for a tour and are using the Marriott as their base.Madgwick also spoke to the team's coach and was shown proof that the group were cricketers."I went out to the protesters and told them, 'You've got it wrong guys, it's a cricket club.' They left within a couple of minutes. It was a massively unfortunate incident," Madgwick told The Guardian.He said the misunderstanding was partly because the coach carrying the players was operated by the same company that had transported asylum seekers who recently arrived in Portsmouth by boat."From the perspective of the people of Portsmouth who are already on high alert, this was a coach from the same company which was turning up with about 40 foreign men," Madgwick said.The incident came after tensions rose in Portsmouth following the arrival of asylum seekers on small boats from France. Hundreds of people, many wearing balaclavas, clashed with police in the city on Sunday evening. Police are investigating possible assaults and criminal damage.A day earlier, crowds dressed in black and wearing balaclavas had blocked a road near the port of Dover. Far-right activist Daniel Thomas, who is closely linked to Tommy Robinson, said he had organised both demonstrations.Madgwick said he understood the concerns of local residents but acknowledged that the incident was far from ideal."It doesn't make our city look like the welcoming city it is. But it's reflective of the climate we live in, and where people are deeply concerned about the issues," he said.Madgwick had earlier posted on Facebook asking people not to go to the hotel after residents contacted him about what they believed were migrants staying there. He later made the post private after it attracted abusive comments.The England and Wales Cricket Board has since contacted the Pakistan Cricket Board to check on the wellbeing of the players and is reviewing security arrangements for the remainder of the team's tour.Pakistan Under-19 recently played England Under-19 in a four-day Test, losing by 10 runs. The teams are scheduled to meet in a one-day match at Arundel on Wednesday, before another ODI in Guildford on Saturday.Pakistan's senior men's team is also currently in England for the third and final Test against England at Edgbaston.
Article Summary: Around 40 people gathered outside the Marriott hotel on Tuesday evening. The protesters had reportedly seen a group of men they believed were asylum seekers. They later discovered that the people staying at the hotel were Pakistan's Under-19 cricket team. The incident came after tensions rose in Portsmouth following the arrival of asylum seekers on small boats from France.

Article Title: ‘The arrow will for sure be a 10’: Jyothi Surekha Vennam’s simple mantra ahead of Asian Games
Article Text:
Jyothi Surekha Vennam

New Delhi:

TOI

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Jyothi Surekha Vennam, the mantra ahead of the Asian Games is deceptively simple: perfect the process and let the scoreboard take care of itself. India’s No. 1 women’s compound archer and a major medal hope, Jyothi will arrive in Aichi-Nagoya for her remarkable fourth Asian Games appearance. At Hangzhou in 2023, she produced a golden sweep, winning gold in the individual, women’s team and mixed team events. She has won medals at every edition of the multisport event.The 30-year-old toldthat her emphasis was on executing each shot cleanly rather than dwelling on expectations. “Right now, I am just focused on myself and on shooting my best. This is the mindset I am going with,” she said, adding, “I’m not chasing results or scores. I know that if I execute my shot really well, the arrow will for sure be a 10.”Jyothi will spearhead a new-look trio featuring Chikitha Taniparthi and Prithika Pradeep, with the team having competed together at World Cups. She is also set to compete in the individual, women’s team and mixed team events, placing her at the heart of India’s campaign. “We are working together as a team to give great performances at the Games. I’m confident about the way things are going right now,” she said,The preparation has been meticulous. At SAI Sonipat, phase two of the national camp has involved archery-specific physical work, two daily practice sessions plus psychology, physiotherapy and gym work.The squad leaves for Japan on Friday and will spend about 10 days training in Kurobe City before entering the Games village.There is no dramatic technical overhaul. “I haven’t made any changes to my equipment or myself,” said Jyothi, who is supported by and training at the Inspire Institute of Sport (IIS). Her biggest sharpening has been mental: “Reading, visualisation and brief meditation keep me calm and focused.” Her approach is equally practical when sessions falter: analyse execution, check equipment, accept bad days and move forward without surrendering confidence or composure.South Korea remains a formidable rival but Jyothi warns against overlooking other Asian teams, saying surprises can emerge from a field where everyone understands the stakes. “The South Koreans are tough competitiors but you can’t underestimate any other Asian country.Everyone is doing a really great job, working hard.”The stakes are higher than medals as the Asian Games offer Olympic qualification opportunities, including a quota linked to the mixed team compound event, adding significance ahead of the Los Angeles Games.Jyothi also spoke about the disappointment of another Khel Ratna snub and said it’s natural for an athlete to “feel bad”. “But I can’t let things that are personal affect the team as a whole,” she said.
Article Summary: Jyothi Surekha Vennam is India's No. 1 women's compound archer. She has won medals at every edition of the multisport event. The 30-year-old will compete in the individual, women’s team and mixed team events.

Article Title: Avinash Sable eyes Asian Games double, 5,000m qualification in Indian Athletics Series final
Article Text:
Avinash Sable

New Delhi:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

With an Asian Games double in his sights, Avinash Sable will put his steeplechase skills to the test at the Indian Athletics Series final here on Thursday while also chasing the 5,000m qualification mark of 13:39.18 seconds.The Athletics Federation of India (AFI) is seeking approval from the Aichi-Nagoya Games organisers for Sable to contest the 5,000m alongside his confirmed 3,000m steeplechase event. But the Hangzhou Asian Games gold medallist must first breach the AFI qualification mark at the JLN stadium.“I am looking forward to evaluating my skills in Thursday’s race before the Japan Asian Games,” Sable said on Wednesday. “Negotiating water jumps in the steeplechase race is an important part of the strategy,” he added.It has been nearly 14 months since the national record holder last competed in the gruelling event featuring seven water barriers and 28 fixed hurdles. Sable suffered an injury at the 2025 Monaco Diamond League and has since undergone rehabilitation.“I’m mentally and physically strong enough to face any challenge during the Games,” he said. Sable won steeplechase gold and 5,000m silver at the Hangzhou Games in 2023 and hopes to win two medals in Japan. His national record is 8:09.91, set at the 2024 Paris Diamond League.Attention will also be on the quartermilers and the women’s 4x400m team.
Article Summary: Avinash Sable will compete in the 5,000m at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. Sable won steeplechase gold at the Hangzhou Asian Games in 2023. The national record holder last competed in the gruelling event 14 months ago.

Article Title: Injury forces Commonwealth Games silver medallist Rishikanta out of Asian Games
Article Text:
India's Rishikanta Singh (PTI Photo)

Kolkata:

TOI

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Manipur’s Rishikanta Singh Chanambam, who won a silver medal in the men’s 60kg weightlifting competition at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, has been forced to pull out of India’s Asian Games squad because of an injury.Speaking toon Wednesday from Manipur, Rishikanta said, “I had been dealing with pain on the left side of my knee even during the Commonwealth Games. I really wanted to compete in the Asiad too because it’s a big competition for me, but I couldn’t manage it. I later consulted a doctor, who said there was a muscle imbalance on my left side. Right now, I’m focusing on my recovery.”Rishikanta was the lone male athlete in India’s weightlifting squad for the continental meet, which will be held in Aichi Prefecture and Nagoya, Japan, from Sept 19 to Oct 4.Besides Rishikanta, the four other athletes who’s been named in the squad were Mirabai Chanu (women’s 49kg), Gyaneshwari Yadav (women’s 53kg), Seram Nirupama Devi (women’s 61kg) and Harjinder Kaur (women’s 69kg).At the last Asian Games, India had sent a two-member weightlifting team comprising Mirabai and Bindyarani Devi, but neither finished on the podium. Mirabai finished fourth in the 49kg category, while Bindyarani was fifth in the 55kg category.Rishikanta will be gutted to miss the Games after his success in Glasgow. Following his performance there, he had said that, had it not been for the injury, he would have gone for gold.Malaysia’s Bin Kasdan Mohamad Aniq eventually won the event with a Games-record total of 273kg. Rishikanta lifted a total of 264kg. He equalled Bin Kasdan’s 121kg in the snatch but could manage only 143kg in the clean and jerk, compared to the Malaysian’s 152kg.For now, the 21-year-old is keeping his focus on recovery, hoping to return stronger and make up for the opportunity he has missed.
Article Summary: Rishikanta Singh Chanambam won a silver medal in the men’s 60kg weightlifting competition at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. The 21-year-old had been dealing with pain on the left side of his knee even during the Games.

Article Title: IOA forms committee to probe Asunta Lakra’s harassment charge
Article Text:
IOA forms committee to probe Asunta Lakra's sexual harassment charge against top HI official

Kolkata:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president PT Usha’s decision to constitute an independent inquiry committee to examine former India women’s hockey captain Asunta Lakra’s complaint has been welcomed by Hockey India (HI) executive board member and vice-president Asima Ali, who called for “strict and immediate action” against those found responsible.Lakra had alleged in her email to Union sports minister Mansukh Mandaviya, the Sports Authority of India (SAI) and TOPS officials in July that, after informing the Jharkhand govt about allegations of sexual harassment against former Eklavya Hockey Centre coach Sudhir Golla, she was threatened by HI secretary general and Hockey Jharkhand president Bhola Nath Singh for speaking up.“It’s a great step. I’m very happy with what Ma’am PT Usha has done. It should have been done earlier, but at least they have done it now. Strict and immediate action should be taken against the culprits,” Ali said.In a letter dated Sept 7, IOA informed HI that it had constituted the committee following the federation’s request to the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports on July 15 and the ministry’s subsequent request to IOA on July 16.The committee will be chaired by retired Justice Deepa Sharma, with Vandana Rao, Mamta Kharb and Sitwat Nabi as members.IOA said the committee would function independently and impartially. HI has been asked to bear the committee’s honorarium and expenses, including travel, accommodation and incidental expenses.IOA president Usha’s letter to HI also stated, “Hockey India is also requested to extend its full cooperation to the Committee and to ensure that all relevant records, documents, information and such other assistance as may be required are made available to the Committee in a timely manner, so as to enable it to discharge its mandate effectively and expeditiously.”Ali said she would extend her full support to the committee and cooperate with its proceedings. “The committee has my complete support. Asunta is also there. I don’t know about the rest,” she said.The HI vice-president also criticised attempts to silence people within the sport before adding, “Bhola Nath should be investigated for allegedly using Hockey India funds for the case that I have filed against him in the Delhi High Court, and the amount should be recovered immediately by Hockey India.”Singh has already denied the allegations made by Lakra, calling them baseless. Golla has also rejected the allegations and demanded a fair inquiry.The dispute between HI and Lakra took a further turn when HI’s Ethics Committee, headed by retired Justice Raghvendra Kumar, initiated a fact-finding inquiry into complaints filed against Lakra by Jharkhand player Albela Rani Toppo. Lakra termed the move “intimidation” and urged the sports minister to intervene and stop the Ethics Committee inquiry against her.With IOA now setting up an independent committee to examine Lakra’s allegations, the focus will be on whether the inquiry brings clarity to the competing complaints and establishes accountability.
Article Summary: IOA forms committee to probe Asunta Lakra's sexual harassment charge against top HI official. Lakra had alleged in her email to Union sports minister Mansukh Mandaviya, the Sports Authority of India (SAI) and TOPS officials in July.

Article Title: Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi’s loss ends India’s junior singles challenge
Article Text:
Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New York City: India’s Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi, the 15th seed, saved four match points after fighting back from a set and a break down in the decider, but could not complete the comeback, going down 3-6, 7-5, 5-7 to Russian qualifier Arina Malygina in two hours and 16 minutes in the US Open girls’ singles second round.Malygina, ranked 104, has an unorthodox game. The 18-year-old uses a generous dose of underspin from the back of the court, chipping her returns and taking pace off the ball whenever the rallies pick up, before suddenly producing some clean ball-striking of her own.Maaya, 17, doesn’t hold back. She likes to go for her shots, a strategy that is likely to pay off when she plays the pros, but in the juniors there is always the risk that the error count keeps climbing.On Tuesday, Maaya was clocking upwards of 110 mph on her first serve for most of the match, but also had 10 double faults. She fought back from 1-3 and 3-5 in the third set, with all five of Malygina’s match points coming on Maaya’s serve, two in the 10th game and three in the 12th.“I felt like my level dropped today. She played great, I don’t want to take anything away from her. She found ways to win the match,” Maaya said.“She played important points better than me. It was a very close match and whoever managed to handle that situation better would come through, she did that better than me.”She added, “I should have gone for my serves in the third set, the speed dropped to 95 mph in some games.”Meanwhile, in the boys’ doubles, India’s Arnav Paparkar and Thailand’s Kunanan Pantaratorn fell to American Safir Azam and Kazakhstan’s Damir Zhalgasbay 4-6, 2-6.
Article Summary: India’s Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi, the 15th seed, saved four match points after fighting back from a set and a break down in the decider. But she could not complete the comeback, going down 3-6, 7-5, 5-7 to Russian qualifier Arina Malygina in two hours and 16 minutes.

Article Title: ‘No parent is comfortable’: K Humpy pinpoints hurdle holding girls back in chess
Article Text:
Indian chess grandmaster Koneru Humpy (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bengaluru: K Humpy, India’s first-ever woman chess player to attain a Grandmaster title, has witnessed dramatic changes to the landscape of the cerebral sport over the last 30-odd years.“Chess was not a commercial sport and women’s chess was not at all (commercial). So even after I became a GM, after being women’s world No. 2 for many years, there was not much money involved in the sport. When I won the Grand Prix, I think my prize money was about 6,000 euros,” said 39-year-old Humpy after her team Alpine APL Pipers, led by Magnus Carlsen on the top board, defeated Mumba Masters 11-6 in the Global Chess League (GCL) on Wednesday.“Now, you have Cairns Cup and Norway Chess, where the first prize for women is about 60,000 euros. The Tata Steel Rapid & Blitz event in India also gives equal prize to women, plus starting fees (appearance money). Sport is becoming more commercial. So, if you have the talent, you can sustain professionally.”Still, very few U-15 girls the world over belong to the Elo 2000 rating bracket, only about 60 compared to 850 boys.Asked what is stopping the vast majority of girls who shine at the age-group girls’ events but remain far off from the GM title, Humpy said: “The major difference is that the parents give more freedom to boys to go to any chess club or to someone’s house. So, they’ll sit with other boys and male players and start working. But when it comes to teenage girls, no parent is comfortable sending a girl alone.“If we have regular training camps where the girls will come and attend along with other boys and with some International Masters or GMs, they’ll definitely pick up fast. I don’t know who can do it, state body, (national) federation or maybe some private parties,” Humpy said.Results (Day 5): APL Pipers 11 bt Mumba Masters 6, Triveni Kings 3 lost to Ganges Grandmasters 15, Mumba 6 lost to Alaskan Knights 11, American Gambits 8 bt Triveni 5.
Article Summary: Koneru Humpy is India’s first-ever woman chess player to attain a Grandmaster title. Alpine APL Pipers, led by Magnus Carlsen on the top board, defeated Mumba Masters 11-6 in the Global Chess League.

Article Title: Tilak Varma’s Duleep Trophy dream run ends at 99, but Test goal remains
Article Text:
South Zone's Tilak Varma (PTI Photo)

Chennai: Tilak Varma was finally dismissed in this year’s Duleep Trophy, falling agonisingly short of a second century. Despite being dismissed for 99, the South Zone captain’s red-ball ambitions stay intact, even though his team is staring at a big loss against East at the MA Chidambaram Stadium.Tilak, who had scored a century and a half-century in South Zone’s semifinal win against North Zone without being dismissed, battled through the Chennai heat on Wednesday against a quality East Zone attack. He was the last man to fall, giving a return catch to off-spinner Kounain Quraishi, as South were eventually bowled out for 336, conceding a massive 372-run first-innings lead.East, opting to bat again rather than send their bowlers back out, were 212-5 at stumps on Day Four, stretching their lead to 584.For Tilak, however, the larger picture remained clear. The 23-year-old left-hander has made no secret about his desire to play Test cricket for India.“I always say to everyone that I want to play red-ball cricket for India, that’s my biggest goal. As a kid, I thought I would play Test cricket first and then white-ball cricket. Red-ball cricket has always been my favourite, it’s my ‘A’ game,” Tilak said.“Over the last five-six years, I have played a lot of white-ball cricket and become good at it.Red-ball cricket is still my favourite, but I am comfortable with both now,” said Tilak.Tilak resumed the day on 56 and immediately took the attack to Mohammed Shami (2-42), striking two boundaries in the opening over. He and Chama Milind took 44 runs from the nine overs of Shami and Mukesh Kumar’s (3-62) combined first spell, putting them under pressure.Shami conceded 25 in his first four overs after giving away only 17 in 11 overs on Day 3.Kishan breaks 16-year-old recordEast’s second innings saw Ishan Kishan continue his first-innings form with 80 off 98 balls, while Shikhar Mohan (52) also remained among the runs.Ishan Kishan amassed 350 runs across both innings of the Duleep Trophy final, surpassing Dinesh Karthik’s aggregate of 333 runs from the 2010 final to set a new record for the most runs in the tournament final.Brief scores: East Zone 708 & 212-5 (I Kishan 80, S Mohan 52; Md Siraj 1-17) vs South Zone 336 (T Varma 99; M Kumar 3-62, Md Shami 2-42, M Quraishi 2-99).
Article Summary: South Zone captain Tilak Varma finally dismissed in Duleep Trophy final. South bowled out for 336, conceding 372-run first-innings lead to East. East opting to bat again rather than send bowlers back out, were 212-5 at stumps.

Article Title: 'There's not many bigger than that': New Zealand cricketer rejects T20 league contract to play India Test series
Article Text:
New Zealand's Mitchell Santner (left) celebrates Virat Kohli's wicket on the third day of the second test match between India and New Zealand at the Maharashtra Cricket Association Stadium in Pune. (PTI File Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Zealand white-ball captain Mitchell Santner has declined a Big Bash League contract from Adelaide Strikers so he can remain available for the Black Caps’ Test assignments against India and Australia.Santner was approached by the Strikers but decided that New Zealand’s international schedule should take priority. New Zealand are set to host India in a full series, including two Tests, from October 22 to December 1 before travelling to Australia for a four-Test series."When you look ahead to the summer we've got, India here for white ball and Tests and Australia away - there's not many bigger than that - it's quite an exciting time. "I'd like to still be part of that," Santner told the 'New Zealand Herald', as quoted by news agency PTI."The offer was good, I'm not going to lie. They knew it would have to be a good offer for me to entertain it with contracting and what would come up."I did entertain the thought of it, but coming back to what we've got coming up, even if I'm not going to play every game of Test cricket, I still feel like there's a role for me," he added.The 34-year-old also wants to continue as New Zealand captain and believes staying with the national team is the better choice for him at this stage of his career."I don't want to give up captaincy. If that was part of the deal, it was a no brainer for me. There were chats that it could have worked. But for me, sitting without a central contract and trying to captain, I don't know if that would sit right at this stage."New Zealand’s centrally contracted players are required to be available for the Super Smash in January, which currently overlaps with the BBL and South Africa’s SA20.Some New Zealand players have instead taken casual contracts, allowing them to play in overseas franchise leagues while still being available for international cricket.Santner said he understood why players were choosing that option, especially because of the difference in earnings between international cricket and franchise tournaments."There's no judgment with guys taking casual deals. We aren't going to keep up with the money for some of these other opportunities going around," Santner said."But for me, I still want to be part of New Zealand cricket and what we've got coming up."
Article Summary: New Zealand white-ball captain Mitchell Santner has declined a Big Bash League contract from Adelaide Strikers. Santner wants to remain available for the Black Caps’ Test assignments against India and Australia. New Zealand are set to host India in a full series, including two Tests.

Article Title: Unbelievable stat! Shubman Gill's solo England tally puts Pakistan's batting crisis in focus
Article Text:
Shubman Gill and Babar Azam (Agency Image)

Pakistan's batting crisis deepens

Another top-order collapse

Pakistan's batting crisis has reached an extraordinary point in their ongoing Test series against England. After three Tests, the entire Pakistan team is now just 11 runs short of the 754 runs Shubman Gill scored on his own during India's five-Test series in England last year.Gill finished India's five-Test campaign with 754 runs, establishing himself as one of the standout performers of the series. Pakistan, meanwhile, have managed 743 runs across the first two Tests and the opening innings of the third Test at Edgbaston.Their latest collapse, when they were bowled out for just 133 on Wednesday, has left Pakistan tantalisingly close to an unwanted statistical milestone.The latest failure came at a particularly turbulent time for Pakistan cricket. Following defeats at Headingley and Lord's, the Pakistan Cricket Board made sweeping changes to the Test setup. Seven players were removed from the squad, while the coaching staff was also sacked as the board attempted to shake up a side that had struggled badly during the series.Yet the changes failed to produce an immediate response at Edgbaston.Asked at the toss how difficult it had been to lead Pakistan through such turbulent circumstances, Babar Azam insisted the situation had not affected him."Not difficult. Yes, after that we had a couple of changes, but I think a good opportunity to new boys, and yes we are trying to do our best in this match," Babar said.The first session, however, suggested that Pakistan's problems had travelled with them to Birmingham.Put into bat, Pakistan lost wickets regularly and were bowled out for 133.Ollie Robinson struck first, trapping recalled opener Saim Ayub lbw for a duck to claim his 100th Test wicket. Jofra Archer then accounted for debutant Azan Awais before Abdullah Shafique fell to Robinson.Shan Masood was next, caught at mid-wicket off Archer after another poor cross-bat stroke.Tongue then took over, dismissing Pakistan captain Babar Azam before removing debutants Ghazi Ghori and Imran Randhawa before lunch.Razaullah Khan fell for 11 in the afternoon session, leaving Saud Shakeel as Pakistan's only meaningful resistance.Shakeel, who had made a fighting 97 in the defeat at Lord's, top-scored again with 43 before Tongue bowled him with a sharp inswinging delivery.Archer finished with 3-25, Robinson took 3-15 from 11 overs and Tongue claimed 4-42 as Pakistan were dismissed for 133.England then extended their advantage in the first innings. Ben Duckett was dismissed for 11 by Mohammad Ali, while Jordan Cox fell for four to Mohammad Abbas. But Emilio Gay and Harry Brook both made fifties to put England in command.The hosts reached 156-4 by stumps, taking a 23-run lead despite Joe Root falling lbw for the 10th time in 13 innings.Robinson was particularly impressive, conceding just 15 runs in 11 overs as he moved from 99 to 102 Test wickets. His Test bowling average of 19.1 is the best among post-war bowlers with more than 100 dismissals.Pakistan's 743 runs across the first three Tests so far make the Gill comparison impossible to ignore. Gill scored 754 runs by himself during India's five-Test series in England last year. Pakistan have needed two complete Tests and one innings of a third to get within 11 runs of that tally. The comparison is a striking illustration of the gulf between individual consistency and Pakistan's collective batting output during this series.
Article Summary: Pakistan are just 11 runs short of the 754 runs Shubman Gill scored on his own during India's five-Test series in England last year. Pakistan have managed 743 runs across the first two Tests and the opening innings of the third Test at Edgbaston. Their latest collapse has left them tantalisingly close to an unwanted statistic.

Article Title: In 1936, an Indian fast bowler's delivery killed a bird at Lord's. The bird was stuffed and mounted on the same ball and now sits in the MCC Museum
Article Text:
Photo credit: X/@HomeOfCricket

The day a cricket ball hit a sparrow

How the sparrow became a museum exhibit

What scientists discovered 84 years later

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The bird has left Lord's only twice

Every corner of Lord's Cricket Ground has a story. Since opening in 1814, the venue in London's St John's Wood has become one of cricket's most iconic grounds. Generations of cricketers have played here, and many of the game's most memorable moments have unfolded on its field.Away from the pitch, Lord's is also home to one of cricket's biggest collections of history. Inside the ground sits the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) Museum, which was inaugurated in 1953 by HRH, The Duke of Edinburgh. It is one of the oldest sporting museums in the world and houses some of the game's most famous artefacts.Visitors can see Kapil Dev's 1983 World Cup-winning memorabilia, the Ashes urn, bats used by WG Grace, and many other pieces of history from different eras of cricket. But among all those exhibits, one display continues to stand out for its unusual story — a cricket ball mounted with a stuffed sparrow.The incident happened on July 3, 1936, during a match between Cambridge University and the MCC at Lord's.Indian fast bowler Jahangir Khan was representing Cambridge University. He was bowling to Tom Pearce when one of his deliveries struck a sparrow in mid-air. The bird died instantly after being hit by the ball.What made the incident even stranger was what happened next. Pearce still managed to play the delivery, and the sparrow fell near the stumps.As recorded by Wisden Almanack: "TN Pearce, the batsman, managed to play the ball and the bird fell against the stumps without dislodging a bail."The unusual moment immediately became part of cricket folklore., and instead of discarding the bird, it was preserved.The sparrow was stuffed and mounted on the very cricket ball that hit it.The display was later placed in the Memorial Gallery at Lord's and has remained one of the museum's most recognised exhibits ever since.The museum describes it as one of its "best-loved artefacts"."The unfortunate bird was stuffed and mounted upon the ball that killed it and subsequently displayed in the Memorial Gallery at Lord's. It has since become one of the most curious and best-loved artefacts ever displayed at the Ground."For decades, thousands of visitors have stopped to look at the sparrow and the ball, making it one of the museum's most talked-about exhibits despite having nothing to do with a famous innings or a major trophy.The sparrow remained on display at Lord's for decades before experts carried out conservation work in 2020.It was sent to London's Natural History Museum, where specialists examined and restored it.The conservation work revealed something that had not been known since 1936. The bird was identified as a young adult male sparrow.The museum also repaired damage that had appeared over time. According to the MCC Museum, "Conservation work at the Natural History Museum in early 2020 revealed for the first time that the sparrow had been a young adult male."The restoration included repairs to skin splits across the abdomen, a loose wing, and cleaning away dust and dirt collected over many years inside the museum.The work was carried out to ensure the exhibit could continue to be displayed for future visitors.The conservation trip in 2020 was only the second time the sparrow had left Lord's since becoming part of the museum.Its first trip came in 2006, when it travelled to the Netherlands.The sparrow became part of the Grand House Sparrow exhibition at the Natural History Museum of Rotterdam, where it was displayed. After returning to Lord's, it continued to occupy its place inside the MCC Museum.The museum noted that the conservation work in London should help preserve the exhibit for years to come."Its more recent trip should guarantee that it remains fit to delight visitors to the MCC Museum for many years to come."
Article Summary: A sparrow was killed by a cricket ball during a match at Lord's in 1936. Instead of discarding the bird, it was stuffed and mounted on the ball that hit it. The display was later placed in the Memorial Gallery at Lord’s. It has remained one of the museum's most recognised exhibits ever since.

Article Title: 'A ball won't kill you, but bullets can': Rashid Khan opens up on his childhood in war-torn Afghanistan

NEW DELHI: From a war-torn nation to making a mark on the world stage, Afghanistan cricket has come a long way. The team has produced stunning performances, challenged some of the best sides in the world and pulled off big wins against top teams. Once seen as minnows, Afghanistan have slowly shed that tag and emerged as a team capable of becoming a nightmare for the opposition.As Afghanistan prepare to face India in a three-match T20I series, starting Sunday at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi, star all-rounder Rashid Khan opened up about the challenges he faced as a child in the war-torn country and how those experiences helped shape his mindset.Rashid is part of the Afghanistan T20I squad for the series against India, with all three matches scheduled to be played in Delhi.During a podcast, with 'The Parenting Pause', Rashid was asked: "You were born into a country which had some level of conflict. There was sort of war. There was some instability. Your memories?"“Well, I think this cricket is just a normal thing, you know. And as I mentioned, what our parents have gone through, when they share their life experience with us, we are, like, you know, so blessed. This is nothing. This pressure is nothing.What we are doing in our life is nothing compared to what they have gone through. You know how it was in Afghanistan 30 years back, 35 years back, and in those days how our parents struggled in the war, like, you know, 40 years back," Rashid said.“My mom and dad, they share their experience — how we went from this place to that place and how hard it was for them to go through all those things. So I was like, they have seen bullets going up in the air. For us to see a ball going up in the air, that is just easy. You know, it won't kill you, but that can kill you. So, to have that kind of mentality — it's just nothing, you just need to go for it — you can do it. You won't die. It's not something that you're going to die from. And you just need to have a strong mindset.Rashid said the mental strength he has developed over the years came largely from watching his parents deal with difficult situations.“And I feel it's all come from my parents. You know, what kind of mindset they had, how strong they were at that particular time, you know, to help and to raise your kids as well in having those kind of tough situations. I think they were the strongest, and I feel like we just got that mentality from our parents.“And whenever facing any tough days, tough time, I just think about how tough that would have been. But they never let themselves down. So why should I let myself down with this pressure?Rashid said remembering what his parents went through helps him put pressure and difficult moments into perspective.“So I think it just all comes mentally, like, you know, to have those things in the mind, and then you become mentally stronger. So yeah, I think I feel I keep that with myself, and it just helps me in a tougher time. It just helps me, and everything just goes in seconds when I think about it. You put everything in perspective. Yeah. So nothing remains.“It's just like, okay, there is a saying now, and they say that what doesn't kill you only makes you stronger.”Rashid believes difficult situations can also become opportunities to learn and grow."It only teaches you and makes you stronger and gives you a better listener. So I think in a pressure situation, tough situation, you know, I'm so happy for that time because it's not only the pressure situation, it's just the best time for me to learn and to get the good experience and to become a better person, physically and mentally," he said.
Article Summary: Afghanistan face India in a three-match T20I series, starting Sunday in Delhi. All-rounder Rashid Khan opened up about the challenges he faced as a child. He said the mental strength he has developed over the years came largely from watching his parents deal with difficult situations.

NEW DELHI: Somewhere on a muddy school field in Haryana right now, a teenager is perhaps drilling the same throwing technique over and over, just as she had watched on television just days ago. Her sole aim is to pull off the one like Sharmila Dhankar, India's Commonwealth Games shot put gold medallist.Before the 2026 CWG campaign, she, like many of us, had almost certainly never heard the name. And it's not because Dhankar had not won anything before the Glasgow Games; she had, a gold medal in the Women's Shot Put F57 event at the 2026 Fazza International Para Athletics Championship, but because one of the primary institutions whose entire job was to carry that story back from the medal podium to villages and training grounds across the state has, for all practical purposes, gone quiet.That's the part of this story that rarely gets told. India walked away from Glasgow with 39 medals, and for a week, the athletes who won them were everywhere, garlanded at airports, seated beside ministers, their faces on the evening news. But medals don't build the next generation of athletes by themselves. Somebody has to keep telling their stories, long after the felicitation photo is filed away, to the kid training in a dusty school ground who needs proof that this path actually leads somewhere.We wanted to know which state sports departments are still doing their job of promoting the sports and their grassroots on their social media platforms, and which ones seem to have simply logged off. So we scrolled through the timelines ourselves. Here's what we found.No state produced more glory in Glasgow than Haryana. Eleven medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze, spanning boxing, wrestling, athletics, and para sport, headlined by a Neeraj Chopra silver that will be replayed on sports channels for years.Alongside him were names most of India still had little knowledge of. The likes of Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Sakshi Chaudhary, Priya Ghanghas, Sachin Siwach, and Ankush Panghal, all of whom trained in government facilities, under government schemes, and who'd probably appreciate their own state department cheering as loudly for them as it does for its concert lineups.Because that's the thing. The Sports Department, Government of Haryana's X account has posted exactly once in all of 2026, and it's a flyer for the music acts playing at the Chief Minister's Cup.Facebook and Instagram follow a similar rhythm with a short cluster of posts around that February event, and then not much else.Eleven medals, and not one dedicated post to show for it. Somewhere in Rohtak or Bhiwani, a young pugilist training in Priya Ghanghas's discipline would probably just like a little proof that someone up top is paying attention.Manipur's page has an odd time-capsule quality to it. This is the state that gave India Mirabai Chanu, one of the country's most beloved Olympic medalists, and this Commonwealth Games alone produced four medalists from Manipur, Chanu's gold among them, alongside Rishikanta Singh, Bindyarani Devi, and Jadumani Singh.And yet the Department of Youth Affairs & Sports' X account hasn't posted since October 2023, a "Run for Unity" event, frozen well before any of this year's medals happened.Although the Facebook page has had a few sporadic posts here and there this year, its Instagram account has managed just two posts since January. It’s the kind of gap that makes you wonder if someone simply forgot the login details somewhere along the way.If there's one number in this whole exercise worth sitting with, it's this: the official Sports Department, Government of Rajasthan hasn't posted on Facebook since April 14, 2012.Fourteen years, through Arundhati Choudhary's Commonwealth gold and everything else that's happened in Rajasthan sport since.Its X account's last original post predates a retweet from March 2021, and there's no Instagram at all. A parallel handle, the Rajasthan State Sports Council, exists across all three platforms and is barely livelier.Somewhere behind Choudhary's medal is a genuinely good story, but it just hasn't found a home on the one page built to tell it.Gulveer Singh managed both a silver and a bronze for Uttar Pradesh this Games, a rare double that would make a great centrepiece for the state's sporting year. Instead, across two separate official handles on three platforms, Uttar Pradesh Sports has produced little beyond reposts, while its sister account, Sports Directorate, Govt of Uttar Pradesh, hasn't posted at all in 2026.Delhi Government, for its part, doesn't run a dedicated sports account at all on any of the popular social media platforms, so gold medalist Harsh Singh and bronze medalist Tejaswin Shankar, both representing India's capital, don't really have an institutional cheerleader online, their wins quietly absorbed into the general churn of city government updates. Both athletes are, in effect, doing their own promotional legwork.Set against all that quiet, Tamil Nadu feels like a different sport altogether. Its Sports Tamil Nadu handles post multiple times a day, celebrating not just its own three medalists, Praveen Chithravel, Selva Prabhu, Muthupandi Raja, but athletes from other states too, weaving in government scheme updates without it ever reading like bureaucracy.Every medallist got a dedicated post. Somewhere in Tamil Nadu, a kid training in long jump or wrestling doesn't have to wonder whether the sport leads anywhere. The state tells them, publicly, almost daily.Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka's Facebook and Instagram pages, Assam, Bihar, and Tripura all follow a version of that same habit, active, consistent, generous with attention toward athletes nobody outside their district would otherwise know existed.Kerala doesn't run a separate sports handle on X but keeps its Facebook and Instagram genuinely lively, making sure Murali Sreeshankar and Mohammed Basil's silvers got their due.Andhra Pradesh mirrors that same rhythm across all three platforms.Not every state falls neatly into being inactive or staying proactive. Punjab's account managed just two posts on X all year, New Year's and Republic Day, though its Facebook and Instagram carry a bit more life around coaching and departmental meetings, even if athletes rarely get top billing.Uttarakhand was genuinely active last year before cooling off in 2026, leaning more toward government scheme announcements on Facebook, though its Instagram at least carried two posts around the Games.Maharashtra has dedicated posts up for both Sarvesh Kushare and Dilip Gavit, with Instagram staying fairly regular, enough effort to stay out of the quiet column.Karnataka's X account hasn't posted since March 2024, around an unrelated cultural-team event, even though its Facebook and Instagram have stayed warm and active toward its CWG medalists.It is worth asking why this actually matters, beyond good manners. Well, a state sports department's social media feed isn't just a courtesy board for congratulations; it's one of the cheapest, most direct tools available to build the next generation of athletes.A youngster in a small town is far more likely to pick up a javelin because they saw a state government post celebrating someone from their own district. Even when it comes to promoting any government policy, social media can be as effective.Visibility drives aspiration. There's a funding logic too. Sponsors, corporates, and even state finance departments allocate resources partly based on visible public interest, and a well-run social account is often the easiest evidence a sport has that interest.ALSO READ: Anahat Singh: What is in the name? A word from Guru Nanak's prayer, now India's squash sensation Silence, on the other hand, sends the message that grassroots sport isn't a priority worth the effort of a single post, even when the state has just produced a medallist on the world stage.It is worth it because sometimes, the first step towards building a sporting culture is simply showing people that their achievements are being seen.
Article Summary: India won 39 medals at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Haryana produced 11 medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze. But the state sports department has posted just once in all of 2026. What do you think is more important for grassroots sports promotion? Government funding or social media presence? Share your view.

Article Title: ‘That video was not ordinary’: PM Modi praises Lovlina for objecting to distorted India map - Watch
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi shares a light moment with boxer Lovlina Borgohain. (PTI Photo)

‘That video was not ordinary’

Mirabai opens up about four difficult years

Narender's joke leaves Modi laughing

NEW DELHI: Boxer Lovlina Borgohain's decision to object to a distorted Indian map during the Commonwealth Games earned special appreciation from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time.Lovlina, who won silver in the women's 75kg category in Glasgow, was among India's medal winners who interacted with Modi at his residence on Sunday. The meeting, attended by Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, Minister of State for Sports Raksha Khadse and Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha, saw athletes recount their experiences from the Games in an informal and emotional setting.In a little over 10-minute video of the interaction shared by the Prime Minister's Office on Monday, Modi brought up Lovlina's confrontation with a restaurant in Glasgow after she noticed a distorted Indian map.“Kya hua wo restaurant waale se jhagda kar rahi thi? (What happened, you were fighting with that restaurant guy?)” Modi asked.Lovlina laughed before explaining why she intervened.“We had such a good performance and it was the last day of the Games. It was a happy occasion sir, we were celebrating and I didn't like it when I saw the distorted map. I politely told them and they have made the changes also,” she explained.Modi applauded the boxer for noticing the issue despite being in the middle of celebrations after her medal-winning campaign.“To be able to recognise the significance of that map at a time when you were celebrating and the Games were over, I can tell you truthfully, that video was not ordinary. It will be remembered by people for a very long time,” he told the Tokyo Olympics bronze medallist.India finished fourth in Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds, with boxing contributing seven gold medals.The interaction also provided an emotional window into Mirabai Chanu's journey to her gold medal in the women's 48kg category. The weightlifter produced a Games-record lift of 190kg, but her triumph came after four difficult years following her one-kilogram miss at the Paris Olympics. Modi asked Mirabai about the tears she shed on the podium and even fed her a laddu during their interaction.“Itne aansu tapak rahe the (So many tears were rolling down),” Modi remarked.Mirabai explained that the tears represented years of accumulated emotions.“I was very happy and emotional at that moment. I was crying because I missed a medal in the Paris Olympics by one kilogram. I have faced a lot in these last four years. I was battling injuries and some family problems too.“There were a lot of things. So, these four years were very tough for me. And when I stood on the podium, our flag went up and the anthem played, it was hard to stop myself,” she said.The meeting also had its lighter moments. Boxer Narender Berwal, who won silver in the +90kg category, recalled a funny exchange with a Pakistani boxer after beating him at the 2015 World Military Games.“During the 2015 World Military Games, I had a bout with a Pakistani boxer. I won it but when we were together in the medical room for treatment to our niggles, he said to me 'Bhaijan aapka naam Narender hai, aapke coach ka naam Narender hai, aapke Pradhan Mantri ka naam Narender hai, mujhe Narender naam se nafrat ho gayi hai.' (Brother, you, your coach and your PM are all named Narender. I hate this name now),” he recalled, drawing laughter from Modi.The Prime Minister also underlined the broader significance of the athletes' achievements, saying their medals were helping inspire a new generation.“I have been in this house for 12-13 years now and if there is one group that I have met regularly here, it is the athletes because of your efforts to win medals for India and your tradition of scaling new heights.“Far more than our push to promote sports in schools, it is your medals that inspire people,” Modi said.
Article Summary: Lovlina Borgohain won silver in the women's 75kg category in Glasgow. Prime Minister Narendra Modi described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time. India finished fourth in Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds, with boxing contributing seven gold medals.

Article Title: ‘From every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping’: PM Modi’s heartfelt message to CWG heroes - Watch
Article Text:
PM Narendra Modi interacted with India's CWG 2026 medal winners at his residence on Sunday. (Pic credit: PM Modi's X post)

Mirabai recalls four years of struggle

‘One family will bring three medals’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s Glasgow success

NEW DELHI: “From every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping.”Prime Minister Narendra Modi had an emotional message for Mirabai Chanu as he interacted with India's Commonwealth Games 2026 medal winners at his residence on Sunday, reflecting on the sacrifices behind the country's successful campaign in Glasgow.Modi hosted the medal-winning contingent at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg and heard athletes recount some of the moments that defined their journeys at the Games. India returned from Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze, finishing fourth in the overall standings.During one of the conversations, Modi recalled the emotional scenes surrounding Mirabai's gold-medal triumph.“Tears were falling from you. I feel as if from every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping,” Modi told the Olympic silver medallist.Mirabai, who won gold in Glasgow, opened up about the difficult journey that preceded her Commonwealth Games triumph, including the disappointment of the Paris Olympics.“I was very happy, and emotional too. That day the happiness was greater and I cried because at the Paris Olympics, I lost a medal by 1 kg. In a player’s life what all we have to face. So within these 4 years, how much and what all I had faced, every time injuries were going on and all that was happening.So with great difficulty I had faced these 4 years. So when all that happened, on the podium when I stood, sir, and when our flag goes up and our national anthem plays, sir, we cannot stop, sir, tears come out on their own,” she said.Modi responded by highlighting the wider impact of the athletes' achievements.“This is very good. It is not as if this achievement of yours is considered only your achievement; your victory becomes a very big inspiration for the coming generations.”The informal interaction also saw athletes share lighter and deeply personal moments from their Glasgow campaigns.Modi reminded para shot put gold medallist Sharmila Dhankar of a promise she had made earlier.“You made a promise. Last time, yours, both daughters will become players,” Modi said with a smile.Dhankar replied: “Haanji, right now they are young in age. In the next Commonwealth, one family will bring 3 medals.”Men's 100m T47 gold medallist Dilip Gavit, meanwhile, spoke about dedicating his performance to his guru.“When I was running, when my event was on 29th (July), that day was Guru Purnima, so that day I gave a gift to my guru,” he was heard saying in the video.In another video posted by Modi, gold medallist boxer Sakshi Chaudhary introduced herself and the contingent.“Hello friends! This is Sakshi Chaudhary. Today, our honourable Prime Minister has invited us, the Commonwealth Games medalists, and we feel very proud. We are extremely happy to have met him; he is very humble. Sir, would you like to say something?” she said.Modi replied with a message that summed up his interaction with the athletes: “Jo khelega, woh khilega” (The one who plays, will blossom). “Always cheer for Bharat.”India's fourth-place finish came despite a significantly smaller contingent and a reduced sporting programme compared to Birmingham 2022. India sent 122 athletes to Glasgow, compared to 210 in Birmingham, while 30 of its 61 medals in 2022 came in sports that were not part of the Glasgow programme.Despite those limitations, India retained its fourth-place position and improved its medal conversion rate, with 38 athletes returning home with medals. Long-distance runner Gulveer Singh was the only Indian athlete to win two medals.The Glasgow Games concluded after 11 days, with Scotland handing over the Commonwealth Games flag and ceremonial baton to India ahead of the 2030 edition in Ahmedabad.The symbols were handed to Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra, Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha and Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi during the closing ceremony.Ahmedabad will become only the second Indian city to host the Commonwealth Games after New Delhi staged the 2010 edition.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi hosted medal-winning contingent at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg. Modi heard athletes recount some of the moments that defined their journeys. India returned from Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze.
